title: Nonconstancy detected at the generic point of a smooth curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $T$ be an integral $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $C$ be a smooth integral $k$-curve of dimension one [def-sc-curves]. Let $\eta_T,\eta_C$ be their generic points [def-sc-generic-point]. For any $k$-morphism $u:T\to C$,
$$u(\eta_T)=\eta_C\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{there is no }k\text{-point }c:\operatorname{Spec}k\to C\text{ with }u=c\circ s_T,$$
where $s_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the structure morphism and a $k$-point means a section of the structure morphism of $C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. If $u(\eta_T)\ne\eta_C$, its entire set-theoretic image is the single closed point $y=u(\eta_T)$, its residue field is $\kappa_C(y)=k$ [def-weil-residue-field], and $u$ factors through that $k$-point. If $u(\eta_T)=\eta_C$, its local-ring map is an injective $k$-homomorphism $u^*:k(C)\hookrightarrow k(T)$ [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], sending each germ near $\eta_C$ to the germ of its pullback.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps), paragraph before the theorem and third proof paragraph, nonconstant maps send generic point to generic point. Extracts old steps 3, 4 and the nonconstancy test at the end of steps 7 and 9.

proof.text: Put $y=u(\eta_T)$. Every point $t\in T$ belongs to $\overline{\{\eta_T\}}$, so continuity gives $u(t)\in\overline{\{y\}}$. If $y\ne\eta_C$, the irreducible closed subset $Z=\overline{\{y\}}$ is proper in $C$, by uniqueness of generic points. If $z\in Z$ were different from $y$, sobriety would give the strict chain $\overline{\{z\}}\subsetneq Z\subsetneq C$, of length two. This contradicts $\dim C=1$. Thus $Z=\{y\}$ is closed and the image of $u$ is exactly $\{y\}$.

source.place: Tag 0BY1, theorem-curves-rational-maps, third proof paragraph: justify the generic-point assertion by dimension and continuity.

proof.text: Assume $y\ne\eta_C$. Since $C$ is of finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$, the structural map $a:k\to\kappa_C(y)$ is an isomorphism. The canonical residue-field point $i_y:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_C(y)\to C$ is a closed immersion: on any affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the closed point $y$, it is the quotient map $A\to A/\mathfrak m=\kappa_C(y)$; on affine opens avoiding $y$ its inverse image is empty. These descriptions satisfy the affine criterion for a closed immersion. Define $c=i_y\circ\operatorname{Spec}(a^{-1})$. Its composite with the structure map of $C$ is the identity, since that composite is induced by $a^{-1}\circ a$. Thus $c$ is a $k$-point with closed image $\{y\}$.

source.place: Tag 0BY1, paragraph defining constant morphisms; Morphisms Tags 01TB (lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points), 01TF (lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type); the residue-field point is the affine quotient.

proof.text: The integral scheme $T$ is reduced. Step 1 places its image inside the closed immersion $c:\operatorname{Spec}k\to C$ from step 2, so reduced-source factorization supplies $v:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ with $u=c\circ v$. Applying the structure morphism $s_C$ gives $s_T=s_C\circ u=s_C\circ c\circ v=v$. Hence $u=c\circ s_T$, with no finite-type assumption on $T$.

source.place: Tag 0356 (lemma-map-into-reduction), applied to the closed residue-field point constructed in step 2.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $u=c\circ s_T$ for a $k$-point $c$, and write $z=c(\operatorname{Spec}k)$. The induced field maps $k\to\kappa_C(z)\to k$ have identity composite. The second map is injective; for $b\in\kappa_C(z)$ its image in $k$ therefore shows $b$ equals the image of an element of $k$. Thus $\kappa_C(z)=k$ as a structural extension, in particular it is finite. The closed-point criterion for finite-type schemes makes $z$ closed. It cannot equal $\eta_C$: a closed generic point would make $C$ a singleton and have dimension zero. Thus $u(\eta_T)=z\ne\eta_C$. Together with step 3 this proves the required equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0BY1, paragraph before theorem-curves-rational-maps; Morphisms Tag 01TF (lemma-closed-point-fibre-locally-finite-type), reverse direction.

proof.text: Finally assume $u(\eta_T)=\eta_C$. The generic stalks of the integral schemes are the fields $k(C)$ and $k(T)$. The stalk homomorphism of the scheme morphism gives $u^*:\mathcal O_{C,\eta_C}\to\mathcal O_{T,\eta_T}$. It commutes with the structural maps from $k$, because $u$ is a $k$-morphism. A unital homomorphism of fields is injective: if a nonzero $b$ mapped to zero, applying it to $bb^{-1}=1$ would give $0=1$. By the definition of the stalk map, the germ of a section maps to the germ of its pullback. This proves every assertion about $u^*$.

Its statement is byte-identical to the live unsplit node and the delivery adds no new nodes; there is no re-split note. Step 1 is correct: continuity puts u(T) inside the closure of {y}, and uniqueness of generic points (lem-sc-scheme-sober) plus dim C=1 force that closure to be {y}, which is closed. Step 2: lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base gives k≅κ(y). The map i_y is a closed immersion by the affine criterion (A→A/m around y, empty preimage elsewhere). c=i_y∘Spec(a^{-1}) has the right direction and s_C∘c=id. Step 3: T is reduced, so Stacks 0356 (schemes.tex l.2269), through the reduced-source factorization node, gives a factorization v, and v=s_T. Step 4: residue maps k→κ(z)→k compose to the identity, so κ(z)=k is finite and z is closed by lem-kun-closed-point-field (a) (Stacks 01TF). A closed generic point would give dim C=0, so z≠η_C. Step 5: the generic stalks are fields (integral clause of lem-sc-rational-functions-generic-stalks; k(T) for any integral T by def-sc-function-field). The stalk map is a k-linear field map, hence injective, and acts on germs by pullback. Stacks 0BY1 (curves.tex l.152-205), including its third proof paragraph, was checked. Edge cases: T=Spec k is constant; T=Spec k(C) is generic and shows T must not be assumed of finite type; Frobenius is generic; nonreduced Spec k[ε] shows why reduced is needed. lean.statement: theorem curve_nonconstant_generic_criterion (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (T C : Scheme.{u}) (sT : T ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sC : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral T] [IsIntegral C] [IsCurve sC] [Smooth sC] (hCdim : topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (u : T ⟶ C) (hu : u ≫ sC = sT) : (u (genericPoint T) = genericPoint C ↔ ¬ ∃ c : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C, c ≫ sC = 𝟙 _ ∧ sT ≫ c = u) ∧ (u (genericPoint T) ≠ genericPoint C → IsClosed ({u (genericPoint T)} : Set C) ∧ Set.range u = {u (genericPoint T)} ∧ Function.Bijective (sC.residueFieldAlgebraMap (u (genericPoint T))) ∧ ∃ c : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C, c ≫ sC = 𝟙 _ ∧ sT ≫ c = u) ∧ (∀ h : u (genericPoint T) = genericPoint C, Function.Injective (u.functionFieldMap h).hom ∧ ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ sC.appTop ≫ C.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint C) trivial ≫ u.functionFieldMap h) = ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ sT.appTop ≫ T.presheaf.germ ⊤ (genericPoint T) trivial) ∧ ∀ (U : C.Opens) (hU : genericPoint C ∈ U) (a : Γ(C, U)), u.functionFieldMap h (C.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint C) hU a) = T.presheaf.germ (u ⁻¹ᵁ U) (genericPoint T) (Eq.mpr (congrArg (fun x : C ↦ x ∈ U) h) hU) (u.app U a))
